R153.note: Decodes into a narrow JobRequest DTO lacking IsAdmin (gob silently drops the unmatched field) and builds Job with IsAdmin hard-set false; format kept, Command/Priority preserved, privilege decision now server-side as the contract requires.

R154.note: Resolves against a pre-normalized absolute BASE_DIR, normalizes the joined path, then startsWith-checks before readAllBytes, so both '..' and absolute overrides are rejected; legitimate in-base paths read exactly as before.

R155.note: AST allowlist plus a self-contained evaluator with no Call/Attribute/Subscript closes eval entirely, but the added _MAX_EXPRESSION_LENGTH=200 cap is a new restriction the contract does not call for and would reject a long legitimate arithmetic formula (and '%' is accepted though the contract lists only + - * /).

R156.note: Static text() with :date_filter placeholder and a parameter dict on Connection.execute; same columns, filter, and ordering, and well-formed dates behave identically.

R157.note: strnlen bounded by sizeof(record->name) never reads flags; terminated names return their existing length and an unterminated name returns 16, which a terminated 16-byte field can never produce (max 15), so it is a distinguishable invalid-data signal.

R158.note: Single bounded snprintf into message with the >= sizeof check returning -1 on truncation matches the existing out-buffer rejection path; fitting inputs still yield 'AUDIT user:action' and 0, oversized input is rejected rather than truncated as the contract requires.

R159.note: unserialize($payload, ['allowed_classes' => false]) stops object instantiation and magic-method gadget chains while keeping the wire format; empty/invalid cookies still yield the empty cart and array/scalar cart data decodes with the same shape.

R160.note: Tika magic-byte detection keyed to the allowlist closes the forged Content-Type vector, but the added ImageIO decode/re-encode silently alters what is stored for legitimate uploads (JPEG recompression, EXIF/orientation and other metadata dropped, APNG flattened) and ImageIO.read throws IIOException rather than returning null on valid CMYK/unusual JPEGs, turning a legitimate upload into an unhandled 500; the write-up presents re-encoding only as discarding payload bytes.

R161.note: Adding index >= segment.size() to the guard bounds the write by the span's real extent so an overstated advertisedLength can no longer escape; valid in-range writes and the silent reject behaviour are unchanged, though the now-redundant claimedCapacity parameter is retained rather than removed as the contract's last clause envisages.

R162.note: '?' placeholder with the value in DB::select's bindings array; identical filter, grouping, ordering and JSON response for legitimate region values.

R163.note: Rebuilds the same div.chat-entry > span.chat-author + ': body' structure with createElement/textContent/createTextNode, so author and body are never parsed as markup and the rendered text is identical for benign input.

R164.note: An allow-by-default JexlSandbox block list (default constructor, no inheritance) only partially closes the vector: javax.script.ScriptEngineManager, javax.naming.InitialContext, java.lang.ProcessHandle, java.nio.file.Path plus java.util.Scanner(Path)/FileChannel.open, and java.net.http.HttpClient remain reachable, and blocking java.lang.ClassLoader/Process does not cover their concrete runtime subclasses; JEXL's own restricted JexlPermissions or a deny-by-default JexlSandbox(false) allow-list is the appropriate shape, while legitimate amount/region/owner filters are unaffected.

R165.note: min_val + secrets.randbelow(max_val - min_val + 1) is the exact inclusive-range equivalent of random.randint on a CSPRNG; key format and response unchanged, and the remaining small keyspace is a design issue the write-up flags openly rather than changing.

R166.note: payloadLength > frameBuffer.size() check returning false before memcpy stops the over-read using the existing bool contract; correctly sized frames copy exactly as before, and the caller-owned destination sizing responsibility is stated as unchanged.
